$comment: Machine-readable findings for the STIG Manager D-DIL connectivity engineering assessment. Source of truth for the generated tables and summary counts in ddil-assessment.md. Evidence entries are `path:line` or `path:start-end` references into the repository at the assessed commit.

assessment.title: STIG Manager D-DIL Connectivity Cybersecurity Engineering Assessment

confidence_levels.confirmed: Behavior read directly in code at the cited lines.
confidence_levels.inferred: Behavior expected from library or platform defaults that are not set explicitly in the repository; not observed in code.

dependencies.name: OIDC Provider (discovery metadata + JWKS) - API side
dependencies.protocol_port: HTTP or HTTPS per STIGMAN_OIDC_PROVIDER (default http://localhost:8080/realms/stigman); TCP port from the authority URL
dependencies.required_at_startup: Yes. Discovery + JWKS fetch is retried STIGMAN_DEPENDENCY_RETRIES (default 24) times at fixed 5 s; failure sets state 'fail' and the process exits 1.
dependencies.required_per_request: No when the token kid is cached. Yes when an unknown kid is presented (one synchronous refresh). Background refresh at half of STIGMAN_JWKS_CACHE_MAX_AGE (default 10 min); API becomes 'unavailable' once the cache is stale.

dependencies.name: MySQL database
dependencies.protocol_port: MySQL protocol over TCP; STIGMAN_DB_HOST default localhost, STIGMAN_DB_PORT default 3306; optional TLS via STIGMAN_DB_TLS_* (no default)
dependencies.required_at_startup: Yes. Preflight connection retried STIGMAN_DEPENDENCY_RETRIES (default 24) times at fixed 5 s, then version check (>= 8.0.24) and schema migration; failure sets state 'fail' and the process exits 1.
dependencies.required_per_request: Yes. Every authenticated /api request loads the user row and may write lastAccess/lastClaims before the controller runs; all business data is in MySQL.

dependencies.name: OIDC Provider (metadata, authorization endpoint, token endpoint) - browser side
dependencies.protocol_port: HTTPS required in practice (client refuses to run outside a secure context); authority from STIGMAN_CLIENT_OIDC_PROVIDER, falling back to STIGMAN_OIDC_PROVIDER
dependencies.required_at_startup: Yes (application load). The client fetches /.well-known/openid-configuration, then performs an authorization-code + PKCE (S256) flow.
dependencies.required_per_request: No. Needed at access-token refresh (scheduled 10 s before exp) and at re-authentication after a refresh failure, refresh-token expiry, or idle timeout.

dependencies.name: STIG Manager API (REST, /op/state, SSE /op/state/sse, WebSocket /socket/log-socket)
dependencies.protocol_port: HTTP on STIGMAN_API_PORT (default 54000) or HTTPS when STIGMAN_API_TLS_KEY_FILE and STIGMAN_API_TLS_CERT_FILE are set; client path prefix STIGMAN_CLIENT_API_BASE (default 'api')
dependencies.required_at_startup: Yes (application load). Env.js and static assets are served by the API; the state SharedWorker must receive the first SSE event within 5 s and the app blocks until currentState is 'available'.
dependencies.required_per_request: Yes. Every data operation is an XHR with an Authorization: Bearer header; XHRs are silently not sent when no token is held.

dependencies.name: Reverse proxy / ingress controller (optional; required for mTLS/CAC)
dependencies.protocol_port: HTTPS (site-specific, typically TCP 443) on the front side; HTTP/HTTPS to the API on the back side
dependencies.required_at_startup: Yes when deployed - all client traffic, including the SSE stream the client requires at load, traverses it.
dependencies.required_per_request: Yes when deployed. Proxy buffering or short idle timeouts break the SSE, NDJSON streaming, and WebSocket endpoints.

dependencies.name: npm registry / package sources (build time; runtime only if launched via npm start)
dependencies.required_at_startup: No for the container image (CMD runs node index.js directly). Yes if the API is launched with `npm start`, because the `prestart` script runs `npm install`.

dependencies.name: Object storage / other outbound HTTP - none present
dependencies.direction: N/A (no object storage; the only outbound HTTP client in the API is the OIDC discovery/JWKS fetch)
dependencies.protocol_port: N/A. Uploaded files are buffered in API process memory (multer memoryStorage) up to STIGMAN_API_MAX_UPLOAD (default 1073741824 bytes) and never written to external storage.

dependencies.name: Container health probe -> API (loopback)
dependencies.protocol_port: Plain HTTP only (the probe always uses the http module) to localhost:STIGMAN_API_PORT (default 54000); socket timeout option 2 s. Not wired by a HEALTHCHECK instruction in the Dockerfile; the orchestrator must invoke node healthcheck.js.
dependencies.required_at_startup: N/A (probe only). The probe path /api/op/definition is behind the 503 service check, so the probe fails whenever MySQL or the OIDC provider is unavailable. When native API TLS is enabled (STIGMAN_API_TLS_KEY_FILE and STIGMAN_API_TLS_CERT_FILE both set) the listener is HTTPS-only and the plain-HTTP probe can never succeed.

failure_modes.behavior: At startup: discovery is retried 24 times at 5 s (about 2 min), then state becomes 'fail' and the process exits with code 1. Mid-session: scheduled refresh (every cacheMaxAge/2, default 5 min) fails and is retried every 10 s; when the stale timer fires at cacheMaxAge (default 10 min) known keys are cleared, oidc status is set false, state becomes 'unavailable', and all /api requests except /api/op/state receive 503 until a refresh succeeds. Tokens carrying a kid not in cache are rejected with SigningKeyNotFoundError after one failed refresh attempt. That on-demand attempt is refreshCache(false): it clears the pending scheduled-refresh (or 10 s retry) timer before fetching and, on failure, does not re-arm it, so the background refresh chain is dead from that point. Once the stale timer then fires, the service check runs ahead of token validation and short-circuits every /api request with 503, so no request can reach getSigningKey to trigger another fetch; restoring the IdP does not restore the API, which stays 'unavailable' until process restart. The only remaining in-process trigger is an admin authenticating to the /socket/log-socket WebSocket (not under /api, so not gated) with a kid that is no longer cached.
security_consequence: availability loss (fail-closed)
no auth bypass: unknown or stale keys are never trusted
audit-log gap while 503s are returned (transactions are still logged as 503)
no automatic recovery when an unknown kid was presented during the outage: 503 persists after the IdP returns until restart (CP-10)

failure_modes.behavior: JWKS requests use a hard 10 s socket timeout; a timeout counts as a failed refresh. An unknown-kid lookup blocks the request for up to 10 s on the refresh before rejecting the token. The startup discovery fetch (undici) sets no explicit timeout, so a black-holed connection can consume the whole retry budget on a single attempt (inferred: undici defaults apply).
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for timeout value; inferred for undici default behavior
security_consequence: latency amplification on unknown-kid requests
premature 'unavailable' if RTT exceeds 10 s
no bypass risk

failure_modes.behavior: A failed scheduled refresh is retried every 10 s; the stale timer is only armed after a successful update, so the cache remains valid for cacheMaxAge after the last success. Recovery is automatic: the next successful refresh emits cacheUpdate, oidc status returns to true and state returns to 'available'. Unknown kids seen during an outage are cached as 'unknown' sentinels that survive both the stale clear and successful refreshes (clearCacheKeepUnknown runs in both paths); a sentinel is overwritten only when a later successful JWKS fetch publishes that kid (setKey replaces the Map entry). Because a cached sentinel never triggers an on-demand refresh, a token signed with a key that was probed during the outage stays rejected until the next scheduled refresh (up to cacheMaxAge/2, default 5 min) after connectivity returns; a kid that is never published stays rejected until process restart. The automatic recovery above holds only while a scheduled refresh (or its 10 s retry) is still armed. The on-demand refresh for an unknown kid is refreshCache(false), which clears that timer before fetching and does not re-arm it on failure. If the fetch fails (IdP still down) there is no longer any scheduled JWKS request: recovery then depends on a later on-demand refresh succeeding, which can happen only while the API is still 'available' (a different, previously unseen kid arrives before the stale timer fires, or an admin authenticates to the ungated /socket/log-socket endpoint). After the stale timer fires, /api requests are short-circuited with 503 before token validation, so a brief IdP outage that coincided with a single unknown-kid request leaves the API 'unavailable' until restart even though the IdP has returned.
security_consequence: stale-key risk bounded by STIGMAN_JWKS_CACHE_MAX_AGE (default 10 min): a key revoked at the IdP remains trusted until refresh
IdP key rotation during an outage causes user lockout until the first scheduled refresh after connectivity returns (not merely until connectivity returns)
a single unknown-kid request during a transient outage converts a self-healing degradation into an outage that requires operator intervention (CP-10)

failure_modes.behavior: JWKS documents are small (a few KB) and are fetched at most every cacheMaxAge/2 plus on unknown kids; bandwidth is not a limiting factor unless throughput is so low that the 10 s timeout is hit. No compression or conditional (ETag) requests are used.
security_consequence: none beyond FM-02 when the 10 s budget is exceeded

failure_modes.behavior: At startup: preflight retried 24 times at 5 s, then 'fail' and exit 1. Mid-session: db status is set false only when the pool emits 'remove' and the pool has become empty; a restore is attempted every 20 s (preflight + version check + schema check). While unavailable, /api requests return 503 with the state object. In-flight queries fail with a MySQL driver error that reaches the generic error handler as a 500 including the stack trace.
security_consequence: availability loss
information disclosure: 500 responses include err.stack
audit-log gap: request transaction logs still go to stdout, but no business audit trail (review history) can be written
user lastAccess/lastClaims updates lost

failure_modes.behavior: The pool config sets connectionLimit (default 25) and TCP keepalive (10 s initial delay) but no connectTimeout, no per-query timeout, and no acquire timeout. Slow queries therefore hold connections indefinitely; once 25 connections are busy new requests queue inside mysql2 with no bound (inferred: mysql2 default queueLimit 0 = unlimited). Because the client XHR timeout is about 8.3 h (30,000,000 ms), users see hung requests rather than timely errors. Deadlocks are retried 15 times at 200 ms.
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for configuration; inferred for mysql2 queue default
security_consequence: denial of service via connection/queue exhaustion (SC-5)
state remains 'available' so the SSE monitor does not warn users
no data-integrity risk: transactions commit or roll back atomically

failure_modes.behavior: Individual connection drops remove one pooled connection; db status is not changed unless the pool becomes empty, so single failed requests surface as 500 errors while the API still reports 'available'. Multi-statement operations use explicit START TRANSACTION/COMMIT with rollback on error, so partial writes inside one request are not committed. The client import loop is per-asset with no retry: a failed asset is reported and the loop continues, so a batch import can be partially applied.
security_consequence: data-integrity risk at the batch level (partial imports) without an audit marker
information disclosure via 500 stack traces
misleading 'available' state

failure_modes.behavior: Large result sets (checklist exports, review listings) and bulk review POSTs (up to STIGMAN_API_MAX_JSON_BODY, default 31457280 bytes) stream through the pool without pagination limits enforced by the server for most list endpoints. No query timeout means low DB throughput directly extends request duration; requests are not shed.
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for limits; inferred for absence of server-side pagination (not exhaustively verified per endpoint)
security_consequence: resource exhaustion (SC-5)
no integrity risk

failure_modes.behavior: At load: metadata fetch throws 'failed to get' and initialization stops at the loading screen. Mid-session: the access-token timer fires 10 s before exp, clears the access token, and calls refresh; the token endpoint fetch rejects, clearTokens(true) runs, and 'noToken' is broadcast. The UI shows a 'Credentials Expired' modal and all subsequent XHRs are silently not sent because window.oidcWorker.token is null. There is no offline or cached-credential path; tokens exist only in SharedWorker memory.
security_consequence: hard session termination at access-token expiry (fail-closed)
no stale-token risk: expired tokens are discarded client-side and rejected server-side
usability: unsaved work cannot be submitted

failure_modes.behavior: The refresh is attempted exactly once, 10 s before exp, with the browser default fetch timeout (no AbortController). At timer fire clearAccessToken() nulls only the worker's internal copy and does not broadcast noToken, so the page keeps its last broadcast token (init.js updates window.oidcWorker.token only from worker broadcasts) and continues to send it. If the round trip exceeds the 10 s buffer, requests issued after exp still carry the old token and are rejected by the API with 401 AuthorizeError (jwt.verify, no clockTolerance); requests are not withheld during the refresh. If the fetch ultimately errors, clearTokens(true) broadcasts noToken and re-authentication is required even though the refresh token was still valid.
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for buffer and single attempt; inferred for browser fetch timeout
security_consequence: unnecessary re-authentication under high latency
expired bearer tokens are presented to the API during a slow refresh and correctly rejected (401), surfacing as errors on user actions rather than a silent gap

failure_modes.behavior: A single failed refresh is terminal for the session (tokens cleared, no retry/backoff). Recovery requires the user to complete an interactive re-authentication via popup/iframe/tab/reload per STIGMAN_CLIENT_REAUTH_ACTION (default popup). PKCE verifier and state are stored in localStorage for the re-auth round trip.
security_consequence: session-fixation resistance preserved (fresh PKCE verifier/state per attempt)
user-visible interruption on every transient IdP blip aligned with a refresh window

failure_modes.behavior: OIDC traffic is small (metadata once per load, token endpoint at refresh). The IdP login page assets themselves are outside STIG Manager. No issue unless throughput is low enough to exceed the 10 s refresh buffer (see FM-10).
security_consequence: none beyond FM-10

failure_modes.behavior: At load: Env.js/static assets fail (blank page), or the state worker's EventSource errors and initialization fails with 'API connection error'. Mid-session: in-flight XHRs fail with status 0/13030 and the failure callback runs (SM.Error dialog); the state SSE reconnects every 3 s and broadcasts 'state-error'; SM.ApiState shows an 'API unavailable' modal. No client-side write queue exists: unsaved edits are lost if the page is reloaded.
security_consequence: availability loss
data loss of uncommitted UI edits
no bypass or integrity risk

failure_modes.behavior: Global Ext.Ajax.timeout is 30,000,000 ms (about 8.3 h): a stalled XHR is finite but is not abandoned client-side for roughly a working day, so to the user it appears as an indefinite mask/spinner. The first SSE event must arrive within 5 s or the client refuses to initialize (unless STIGMAN_CLIENT_STATE_EVENTS=false). Server-side, in-flight requests whose client disconnects are logged with clientTerminated=true.
security_consequence: denial of service via hung connections (SC-5)
audit records for client-terminated requests carry status undefined

failure_modes.behavior: Each XHR is fire-once; requestPromise rejects with ExtRequestError and the caller shows an error dialog. Bulk import issues one POST per asset sequentially with no retry or idempotency key; a mid-batch failure leaves earlier assets committed and later assets processed. The failure path only raises a transient SM.Error dialog and continues; updateStatusGrid is called solely on success, and a failed importAsset is caught inside that function, so the status grid carries no row for the failed asset and there is no consolidated record of which assets failed. Review PATCH/POST are individually transactional server-side. SSE auto-reconnects every 3 s.
security_consequence: partial-import data-integrity risk
error dialogs include the server response body (which for 500s includes a stack trace)

failure_modes.behavior: CKL/CKLB/XCCDF files are parsed in the browser and only JSON review arrays are POSTed, which reduces payload size. However, no HTTP response compression middleware is registered (the 'compression' package is declared but not wired), JSON bodies up to 31457280 bytes and multipart uploads up to 1073741824 bytes are accepted, and uploads are buffered entirely in API memory. Large exports are unpaginated.
security_consequence: memory exhaustion on slow large uploads (SC-5)
long transfer windows increase exposure to mid-transfer disconnects (FM-15)

failure_modes.behavior: Equivalent to FM-13 from the browser's perspective. If the proxy is up but the API is down, the proxy returns 502/504; the state worker treats these as errors and retries every 3 s.
security_consequence: availability loss
proxy error pages may disclose proxy software/version (site-dependent, inferred)

failure_modes.behavior: Proxy response buffering delays the first SSE event beyond the 5 s client budget and the client refuses to initialize with a diagnostic message; the API sets X-Accel-Buffering: no to prevent this on nginx. Proxy idle timeouts shorter than the 30 s SSE keep-alive or 30 s WebSocket ping drop long-lived connections repeatedly.
security_consequence: availability loss at application load
operators may be tempted to disable state events (STIGMAN_CLIENT_STATE_EVENTS=false), removing the user-facing dependency-status warning

failure_modes.behavior: SSE and WebSocket sessions are re-established by the client (SSE every 3 s; WebSocket per the log-stream client). REST XHRs are not retried. TLS session resumption and connection reuse are proxy-dependent.
security_consequence: same as FM-15
no session-fixation risk: bearer tokens are re-sent per request, no proxy-side session cookie is used

failure_modes.behavior: Proxy body-size limits (e.g., nginx client_max_body_size) reject large imports before they reach the API; the documentation recommends 100 MB. Without proxy-level compression, unpaginated JSON responses consume the constrained link.
security_consequence: availability loss for large imports
misleading client errors (proxy HTML error page fails JSON parsing -> NonJsonResponse)

failure_modes.behavior: Image builds (npm ci) and client builds (uglify-js, client modules) fail without registry access. A deployment that launches the API with `npm start` fails at `prestart` (npm install) even though node_modules is already present, unless npm resolves everything from local cache. The container CMD (node index.js) is unaffected.
security_consequence: inability to rebuild/patch in a disconnected enclave (CP-10, SR-3)
temptation to disable integrity checks or use unvetted mirrors

failure_modes.behavior: Slow registry access lengthens builds; npm's own retry/backoff applies (inferred: npm defaults). No runtime impact for the container image.
security_consequence: none at runtime

failure_modes.behavior: Partial installs are prevented by lockfile-driven `npm ci` (it fails rather than installs a subset). `npm install` in `prestart` could resolve floating ranges differently across attempts.
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for npm ci semantics; inferred for prestart drift
security_consequence: supply-chain drift if prestart install is used in production (SR-3, CM-6)

failure_modes.behavior: Build-time only; large dependency trees (api/source/package-lock.json) transfer slowly. No runtime impact.
security_consequence: none at runtime

failure_modes.behavior: Not applicable: there is no object store to lose. All persistent data resides in MySQL (DEP-02). Uploaded files are transient in-process buffers.
security_consequence: none

failure_modes.behavior: Not applicable (no external storage round trips).
security_consequence: none

failure_modes.behavior: Not applicable. A multipart upload interrupted mid-transfer is discarded by multer; nothing partial is persisted.
security_consequence: none

failure_modes.behavior: Because uploads are held in memory rather than streamed to storage, a slow upload keeps up to STIGMAN_API_MAX_UPLOAD (default 1 GiB) of process memory committed for the duration of the transfer; concurrent slow uploads multiply this.
security_consequence: memory exhaustion / DoS (SC-5)

failure_modes.behavior: When MySQL or the OIDC provider is unreachable the API is 'unavailable' and /api/op/definition returns 503; the probe exits 1. An orchestrator configured to restart on probe failure will restart the API in a loop for the duration of the dependency outage, each restart re-running the 24x5 s bootstrap and ultimately exiting 1. Independently of dependency state, a deployment with native API TLS enabled presents an HTTPS-only listener while the probe always sends plain HTTP, so every probe fails (exit 1 via the 'error' handler) even when the API is fully healthy; a restart-on-unhealthy orchestrator would then restart a healthy API continuously.
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for probe semantics and the TLS mismatch; orchestrator restart behavior is deployment-dependent (inferred)
security_consequence: prolonged availability loss and restart churn (CP-10)
loss of in-memory JWKS cache and request statistics on every restart
log volume amplification
native TLS (SC-8) and a usable liveness probe are mutually exclusive at the assessed commit

failure_modes.behavior: The probe sets timeout: 2000 but registers no 'timeout' handler and never destroys the request; the option only causes Node to emit a 'timeout' event on socket inactivity, it does not abort the request (inferred: Node http semantics). If the API accepts the connection but never responds (event loop saturated by slow DB work, FM-06), the probe process therefore does not exit after 2 s; it lingers until the socket is closed by another cause or the orchestrator's own probe timeout kills it. Whether a degraded API is then treated as unhealthy depends entirely on the orchestrator's external timeout, not on the 2 s value in the script.
failure_modes.confidence: confirmed for the missing handler; inferred for Node timeout-event semantics
security_consequence: liveness outcome under degradation is undefined by the application and delegated to orchestrator defaults (CP-10, SC-5)
a hung probe process per interval can accumulate if the orchestrator does not enforce its own timeout

failure_modes.behavior: Probe results flap with dependency state; orchestrator failure thresholds determine whether a restart is triggered (deployment-dependent).
security_consequence: restart churn

failure_modes.behavior: Loopback probe is unaffected by external bandwidth.
security_consequence: none

recommendations.title: Bound client request time and fail fast when no token is held
recommendations.recommendation: Replace the global Ext.Ajax.timeout of 30,000,000 ms with a bounded default (for example 60 s, with explicit longer per-request timeouts for exports/imports), surface an explicit error when Ajax.js declines to send because window.oidcWorker.token is null (today the request silently never fires), and add bounded retry with jittered backoff for idempotent GETs.

recommendations.title: Make token refresh tolerant of transient IdP loss
recommendations.recommendation: In the OIDC SharedWorker, start the refresh earlier than 10 s before exp (configurable, e.g., 25% of lifetime), retry a failed refresh with backoff while the refresh token is still valid, and only clear tokens and broadcast 'noToken' when the refresh token itself has expired or the IdP returns a definitive 4xx. Keep the current fail-closed behavior at refresh-token expiry.

recommendations.title: Define the IdP-unreachable policy for the API (JWKS staleness window)
recommendations.recommendation: Decide and document how long the API may keep verifying tokens with last-known JWKS keys when the IdP is unreachable. Today this is STIGMAN_JWKS_CACHE_MAX_AGE (default 10 min, max 35791 min), after which the API fails closed with 503. For enclave deployments, set the value to the mission-approved window, and consider an engineering change that distinguishes 'refresh failed' from 'keys expired' so that revocation latency and availability can be tuned independently. Independently of the policy value, fix the no-recovery branch: getSigningKey calls refreshCache(false), which cancels the scheduled refresh timer and does not re-arm it on failure, so an unknown kid presented during an outage leaves no JWKS request scheduled and the API stays 503 after the IdP returns. Preserve the existing timer across on-demand refreshes (or re-arm the 10 s retry when the on-demand fetch fails), and have the cacheStale handler start a retry loop so an 'unavailable' API always has a pending path back to 'available'.

recommendations.title: Provide a durable audit-log path independent of network log shipping
recommendations.recommendation: Logging is synchronous JSON to stdout with no local buffer or file. Deploy a local log sink (file with rotation, or a sidecar/agent with disk-backed buffering) so audit records survive loss of the network path to the central collector, and configure the orchestrator not to drop container stdout during collector outages. Add an AU-5-style alert when the sink is unavailable. Document the accepted maximum audit gap.

recommendations.title: Remove stack traces and token payloads from failure-path outputs
recommendations.recommendation: The generic error handler includes err.stack in 500 and untyped error responses, which under DB/network faults are the common path; the client then renders that body in an error dialog. Return a correlation id (requestId already exists) instead of the stack, and keep the stack in the server log only. In the default 'combined' log mode the decoded access-token payload is attached to every request log; the OIDC worker also console-logs full token responses. Restrict both to a debug level.

recommendations.title: Add MySQL connect/query/acquire timeouts and error-driven unavailability
recommendations.recommendation: Set connectTimeout, a per-query timeout, and a bounded queueLimit/acquire timeout in the pool config so degraded DB links fail fast. Additionally mark db unavailable (or emit a degraded state) on sustained query errors rather than only when the pool becomes empty, so the SSE state stream warns users before requests hang.

recommendations.title: Make bulk import resumable and idempotent
recommendations.recommendation: The import loop issues one asset PATCH/POST and one review POST per asset with no retry; a mid-batch fault yields a partially applied batch. Add per-asset retry with backoff for network-class failures, an exportable 'not applied' manifest at the end of the run, and (server-side) an optional import-batch identifier recorded in review history so partial batches are auditable and re-runnable.

recommendations.title: Separate liveness from readiness in the container health probe
recommendations.recommendation: healthcheck.js requests /api/op/definition, which is gated by the 503 service check, so any dependency outage makes the container 'unhealthy' and invites restart loops. Point the liveness probe at /api/op/state (always served) and use the 'available' state only for readiness/traffic routing. Make the probe TLS-aware (select https when STIGMAN_API_TLS_KEY_FILE/STIGMAN_API_TLS_CERT_FILE are set, or expose a separate loopback plain-HTTP liveness listener), and add a 'timeout' handler that destroys the request and exits nonzero, following the pattern already used by the JWKS client, so the 2 s budget is actually enforced.

recommendations.title: Publish a D-DIL reverse-proxy profile
recommendations.recommendation: Codify the proxy settings the client depends on (no buffering for /op/state/sse and NDJSON endpoints, read/idle timeouts above the 30 s keep-alive, WebSocket upgrade, body size at least the expected import size, and passing 503 JSON bodies through unmodified) as a tested configuration fragment, and state that STIGMAN_CLIENT_STATE_EVENTS=false is a diagnostic setting, not a D-DIL mitigation.

recommendations.title: Set an explicit JWT clock-skew tolerance
recommendations.recommendation: jwt.verify is called without clockTolerance, so exp/nbf are enforced with zero tolerance; the WebSocket log session likewise computes expiry from local time. Edge nodes with drifting clocks (common when NTP is unreachable) will reject valid tokens or accept them slightly late. Add a configurable clockTolerance (e.g., 30-60 s) and document the NTP requirement.

recommendations.title: Decide the offline-authentication posture (no cached-credential path exists)
recommendations.recommendation: Neither the client nor the API has an offline or cached-credential path; both fail closed when the IdP is unreachable. The assessment recommends against adding cached credentials to the browser client. If disconnected operation is a mission requirement, deploy an IdP instance inside the enclave (with key material and user federation synchronized when connected) and point STIGMAN_OIDC_PROVIDER / STIGMAN_CLIENT_OIDC_PROVIDER at it.

recommendations.title: Enable response compression and cap unbounded payloads
recommendations.recommendation: The 'compression' package is a declared dependency but no compression middleware is registered. Enable it for JSON responses, and review STIGMAN_API_MAX_JSON_BODY (default 31457280 bytes) and STIGMAN_API_MAX_UPLOAD (default 1073741824 bytes, held in memory) against the bandwidth and memory actually available at the edge.

recommendations.title: Remove registry access from the runtime start path and document offline builds
recommendations.recommendation: The `prestart` script runs `npm install`, so `npm start` needs registry access; the container CMD does not. Document `node index.js` (or `npm start --ignore-scripts`) for disconnected hosts, and document an offline build procedure (private registry mirror or vendored lockfile with `npm ci --offline`) with integrity verification.

recommendations.title: Reconcile documented defaults with code
recommendations.recommendation: The environment-variable reference documents STIGMAN_API_MAX_JSON_BODY default 5242880 while config.js uses 31457280. Reconcile so operators sizing proxies and links for D-DIL use the real value.

lab_tests.setup: Compose: mysql:8.0.24, keycloak (or test/api/mock-keycloak), stig-manager API, toxiproxy in front of the API port. Browser points at the toxiproxy listener.
steps: Log in; open a collection.
Add toxic `timeout` (timeout=0) on the API proxy to black-hole responses.
Trigger a GET (e.g., open Assets grid) and observe the UI for 120 s.
Remove toxic; clear the token via IdP session logout and trigger a GET.
lab_tests.pass: The request fails with a user-visible timeout error within the configured bound (<= 60 s default); the no-token case shows an explicit error instead of a silent no-op.
lab_tests.fail: Spinner/mask persists beyond the bound, or no error is shown when no token is held.

lab_tests.setup: Keycloak access-token lifespan 2 min, refresh 30 min. toxiproxy in front of Keycloak.
steps: Log in and wait until 20 s before access-token exp.
Add toxic `timeout` on the IdP proxy for 40 s, then remove it.
Observe the OIDC worker and UI.
lab_tests.pass: Refresh is retried and succeeds after the toxic is removed; no 'Credentials Expired' modal while the refresh token remains valid.
lab_tests.fail: Tokens are cleared and re-authentication is demanded after the first failed refresh.

lab_tests.tooling: docker compose + `docker stop` on the IdP; existing test/state harness pattern
lab_tests.setup: STIGMAN_JWKS_CACHE_MAX_AGE set to the approved window (e.g., 60). Two signing keys: A, published at the IdP when the API starts (so it is cached by setupJwks), and B, added to the IdP's JWKS only after the API has started and before its next scheduled refresh (cacheMaxAge/2), so B is present at the IdP but absent from the API cache. Verify the precondition from the jwksCacheEvent debug log (kids list at startup shows only A); do not present B while the IdP is up, because that on-demand refresh would cache B and defeat run 2.
steps: Run 1 (scheduled path): obtain token A; stop the IdP container.
Call an authenticated endpoint with A every 30 s and record the first 503.
Restart the IdP and record time to 'available' via /api/op/state.

Run 2 (on-demand path): restart the API while only key A is published; obtain token A. Publish key B at the IdP and mint token B without waiting for a scheduled API refresh (well inside cacheMaxAge/2). Stop the IdP. Present B once (expect 401 SigningKeyNotFoundError) so getSigningKey runs refreshCache(false) against the unreachable IdP.
Continue calling with A every 30 s; record the first 503.
Restart the IdP; poll /api/op/state for at least 3 x STIGMAN_JWKS_CACHE_MAX_AGE and record whether 'available' returns without an API restart.
lab_tests.pass: In both runs 503 begins only after the approved window elapses, tokens with unknown kids are rejected throughout, and recovery to 'available' occurs within one refresh interval (<= 10 s retry) after the IdP returns without restarting the API. (At the assessed commit run 2 is expected to fail: no JWKS request remains scheduled after the failed on-demand refresh, so 503 persists until restart.)
lab_tests.fail: 503 occurs earlier than the window, recovery in either run requires an API restart, or any unknown-kid token is accepted.

lab_tests.tooling: docker compose with `healthcheck` stanza, `docker inspect --format '{{json .State.Health}}'`, `docker stop` on MySQL, and a stalled-listener stub (`nc -l` that accepts and never responds)
lab_tests.setup: Compose healthcheck for the API service: `test: ["CMD", "node", "healthcheck.js"]`, interval 10 s, timeout 5 s, retries 3, start_period 120 s. Compose restart policies act only on container exit, not on health status, so restart churn is observed indirectly: record Health.Status / Health.FailingStreak transitions from `docker inspect` (or `docker events --filter event=health_status`) as the signal an orchestrator would act on. Prepare a second API service with STIGMAN_API_TLS_KEY_FILE and STIGMAN_API_TLS_CERT_FILE set.
steps: Case A (dependency outage): stop MySQL for 5 min; sample `docker inspect` Health every 10 s.
Case B (native TLS): start the TLS-enabled API with MySQL and the IdP healthy; run `docker exec <api> node healthcheck.js; echo $?` five times.

Case C (stalled listener): run `node healthcheck.js` with STIGMAN_API_PORT pointed at a stub that accepts the TCP connection and never writes a response; time how long the process lives (bound the run with `timeout 60`).
lab_tests.pass: Case A: Health.Status stays 'healthy' for the whole outage while /api/op/state reports 'unavailable', and the API returns to 'available' within one restore interval (20 s) after MySQL returns. Case B: exit code 0 on all five runs. Case C: the probe exits nonzero on its own within 2 s (+/- 0.5 s) without external kill.
lab_tests.fail: Case A: Health.Status becomes 'unhealthy' (FailingStreak >= retries) during the outage. Case B: any nonzero exit while the API is healthy. Case C: the process is still alive at 3 s or is terminated only by the external `timeout`.

lab_tests.tooling: docker compose + nginx with the published D-DIL profile + `tc netem delay 800ms`
lab_tests.setup: nginx in front of the API using the profile fragment.
steps: `curl -N https://<proxy>/api/op/state/sse` and time the first event.
Hold the SSE connection for 5 min under 800 ms delay.

Through the proxy, `POST /api/stigs?elevate=true` as multipart/form-data with field `importFile` = a valid XCCDF benchmark `.xml` padded with XML comments to about 50 MB (below STIGMAN_API_MAX_UPLOAD, default 1073741824 bytes); this is the one client operation that sends a single large request body, because CKL/CKLB/XCCDF review imports are parsed in the browser and posted as many small JSON review requests. Record the HTTP status and body.
Control: set the proxy body limit to 10 MB and repeat the same POST.
lab_tests.pass: First SSE event within 2 s; the connection survives 5 min with keep-alives every 30 s; the 50 MB importBenchmark request reaches the API and returns the API's own JSON response (200, or a typed 4xx from importBenchmark itself). Control: the 10 MB-limited proxy returns 413 with a non-JSON body, reproducing FM-20.
lab_tests.fail: First event later than 5 s (client refuses to initialize), connection drops before 5 min, or the 50 MB request is rejected by the proxy (413 or a proxy HTML page) before reaching the API.

lab_tests.tooling: docker compose + libfaketime (or `date -s`) inside the API container; tokens minted with test/utils/mockOidc.js getToken (issuedAt/expiresIn) plus a local nbf claim via jsonwebtoken's notBefore option, since not every IdP emits nbf
lab_tests.setup: IdP/minting clock is the reference. All offsets below are the API clock relative to that reference. Run the whole matrix twice: once with the implemented tolerance set to 60 s, once as a control with tolerance 0 s (the assessed-commit behavior). Tokens: T1 = iat = nbf = now, exp = now + 300 s (nbf present); T2 = exp = now - 30 s; T3 = exp = now - 90 s.
steps: API clock -45 s (behind the IdP): present T1. Its nbf is 45 s in the API's future, so acceptance depends only on tolerance.
API clock correct: present T2 (30 s past exp, inside a 60 s tolerance).
API clock correct: present T3 (90 s past exp, beyond a 60 s tolerance).
API clock +45 s (ahead): present T2 again (now 75 s past exp as seen by the API).
Repeat steps 1-4 with tolerance 0 s.
lab_tests.pass: Tolerance 60 s: T1 at -45 s accepted (200); T2 at correct clock accepted; T3 rejected (401); T2 at +45 s rejected. Tolerance 0 s (control): T1 at -45 s rejected (jwt not active); T2 rejected; T3 rejected. Every rejection is a typed 401, never a 500. The two runs must differ exactly on the T1 and T2 rows, proving the setting is wired into jwt.verify.
lab_tests.fail: Any row deviates from the matrix, the 60 s and 0 s runs produce identical results (tolerance not applied), or a rejection surfaces as a 500 with a stack trace.

steps: Compare each default in docs/installation-and-setup/envvars.csv with api/source/utils/config.js.

government_decisions.decision_required: Whether STIG Manager must operate while the enterprise IdP is unreachable, and if so whether the approved mechanism is an enclave-local IdP (recommended) versus any form of cached credentials in the client (not recommended).

Maximum tolerable loss window for audit/transaction records during a network or collector outage, and whether local disk buffering of logs containing user identifiers is permitted in the deployment enclave.
Approved access/refresh token lifetimes, idle timeout values (STIGMAN_CLIENT_USER_TIMEOUT / STIGMAN_CLIENT_ADMIN_TIMEOUT, default 0 = disabled), and the JWT clock-skew tolerance for edge nodes.
How long the API may continue to accept tokens signed with last-known keys after losing the IdP (STIGMAN_JWKS_CACHE_MAX_AGE), balancing availability against revocation latency.

Whether multiple enclave instances may operate on the same collections and, if so, the authoritative source and conflict rule (last-writer-wins by review timestamp vs. manual reconciliation) for reviews and review history imported after reconnection; and whether partial imports must be rolled back or completed.
Whether a read-only or cached-view mode is desired when MySQL is degraded, or whether the current fail-closed 503 posture is acceptable.
Approved level of diagnostic detail in client-visible errors and in default-level operational logs (stack traces, decoded token claims).
